questions.text:
P, Q, R and S are pieces of apparatus.

[DIAGRAM – APPARATUS AND TABLE]
Four labelled apparatus images: P = burette (50 cm³), Q = gas syringe (100 cm³), R = measuring cylinder (50 cm³), S = pipette (25 cm³).
Below: a table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'apparatus', Column 2: 'measurement made'
Row A: P | the volume of acid added to alkali in a titration
Row B: Q | 0.24 dm³ of hydrogen gas produced when magnesium reacts with an acid
Row C: R | 75 cm³ of a gas given off in a rate-determining experiment
Row D: S | 20 cm³ of alkali for use in a titration
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

Which row describes the correct apparatus for the measurement made?

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

X is a mixture of colourless compounds. The diagram shows a chromatogram of X and of three pure compounds, P, Q and R.

[DIAGRAM – CHROMATOGRAM]
A chromatography plate with a horizontal start line at the bottom. Four lanes labelled X, P, Q, R from left to right. Spots visible: X lane has spots at two different heights; P lane has one spot at low height; Q lane has one spot at medium height; R lane has spots at low and high heights. Solvent front visible at top.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which statement is NOT correct?

A  X could contain P and R.
B  Q has a greater Rf value than R.
C  P and R have different solubilities in the solvent.
D  A locating agent was used to develop the chromatogram of X.

Which substance can be distilled using the apparatus below?

[DIAGRAM – DISTILLATION APPARATUS AND TABLE]
A simple distillation setup: round-bottom flask containing a mixture, heated by a water bath with heat source below; thermometer in flask neck; condenser with water-in and water-out labels; collecting vessel for distillate on the right.
Below: a table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'melting point/ °C', Column 2: 'boiling point/ °C'
Row A: −138 | 0
Row B: −123 | 50
Row C: 0 | 108
Row D: 41 | 182
Recommended rendering tool: SVG for apparatus, SVG table for data.

Which substance can be distilled using the apparatus?

A  substance A
B  substance B
C  substance C
D  substance D

Which row about a change of state is correct?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'change of state', Column 2: 'energy change', Column 3: 'process'
Row A: solid → liquid | heat given out | melting
Row B: gas → liquid | heat taken in | evaporation
Row C: solid → gas | heat taken in | sublimation
Row D: liquid → solid | heat given out | condensing
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

The cooling curve for substance X is shown below.

[DIAGRAM – COOLING CURVE]
A line graph. Y-axis: 'temperature/ °C' with markings at 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250. X-axis: 'time/ min'. The curve starts at approximately 200 °C, decreases, levels off at a plateau at 150 °C, continues decreasing, then levels off at a second plateau at 50 °C, before decreasing again toward 0 °C.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

At which temperature does both solid and liquid exist?

A  0 °C
B  50 °C
C  150 °C
D  200 °C

The ion of an element Z is shown below.

[DIAGRAM – ION ELECTRON STRUCTURE AND TABLE]
A dot-and-cross diagram showing a Z³⁺ ion enclosed in square brackets with a 3+ superscript. The ion has two concentric circles: the inner shell has 2 electrons, the outer shell has 8 electrons (shown as crosses), giving a total of 10 electrons.
Below: a table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'group', Column 2: 'period'
Row A: 13 | 2
Row B: 13 | 3
Row C: 15 | 2
Row D: 15 | 3
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

In which group and period does element Z belong to in the Periodic Table?

A  group 13, period 2
B  group 13, period 3
C  group 15, period 2
D  group 15, period 3

Which row includes an element, a compound and a mixture?

A  sea water, tap water, pure water
B  sodium chloride, chlorine, pure water
C  sea water, sodium chloride, chlorine
D  sodium chloride, sea water, pure water

Which row correctly classifies how graphite, aluminium and molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'using mobile ions and electrons', Column 2: 'using mobile electrons only', Column 3: 'using mobile ions only'
Row A: molten sodium chloride | graphite | aluminium
Row B: molten sodium chloride | aluminium, graphite | none of the above
Row C: aluminium | graphite | molten sodium chloride
Row D: none of the above | aluminium, graphite | molten sodium chloride
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

The diagram shows the results of a pH test on a sample of garden soil.

[DIAGRAM – pH SCALE]
A horizontal pH scale from 3 to 11 with tick marks at each integer. An arrow labeled 'soil reading' points downward to pH 4.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

What could be added to the soil to change its pH to 7?

A  calcium oxide
B  sodium oxide
C  sodium chloride
D  ammonium nitrate

The graph shows how pH changes as 0.1 mol/dm³ of dilute sodium hydroxide is gradually added to 0.1 mol/dm³ of ethanoic acid.

[DIAGRAM – GRAPH AND TABLE]
A line graph. Y-axis: 'pH' (0 to 14). X-axis: 'volume of NaOH used/ cm³' (0 to 50). The titration curve starts at approximately pH 4, rises gradually, then sharply at around 25 cm³, and levels off at approximately pH 13.
Below: a table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'indicator', Column 2: 'colour change', Column 3: 'pH at which colour change occurs'
Row A: crystal violet | yellow → violet | 0.0 – 2.0
Row B: methyl orange | red → yellow | 3.1 – 4.4
Row C: phenolphthalein | colourless → pink | 8.3 – 10.0
Row D: indigo carmine | blue → yellow | 11.4 – 13.0
Recommended rendering tool: image generator for graph, SVG table for data table.

Which indicator is most suitable to be used in the titration to identify the end-point of neutralisation?

A  crystal violet
B  methyl orange
C  phenolphthalein
D  indigo carmine

Copper(II) sulfate is made by reacting excess insoluble solid M with solution N.

Which row identifies M and N and the method used to extract crystals of copper(II) sulfate from the mixture?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'M', Column 2: 'N', Column 3: 'method'
Row A: copper | sodium sulfate | filter the mixture to obtain the residue
Row B: copper | sulfuric acid | filter the mixture and evaporate filtrate until crystals form
Row C: copper(II) oxide | sulfuric acid | filter the mixture to obtain the residue
Row D: copper(II) carbonate | sulfuric acid | filter the mixture and evaporate filtrate until crystals form
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

Which of the following pairs of gases changes the colour of damp red litmus paper?

A  ammonia and chlorine
B  ammonia and carbon dioxide
C  chlorine and hydrogen
D  chlorine and sulfur dioxide

The diagram shows the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide.

[DIAGRAM – ELECTROLYSIS APPARATUS AND TABLE]
A circuit diagram: a battery/power supply connected to two electrodes (electrode X on the left, electrode Y on the right) dipping into a container of molten lead(II) bromide. A heat source is shown below the container.
Below: a table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'electrode X', Column 2: 'electrode Y'
Row A: brown gas | grey metal
Row B: colourless gas | grey metal
Row C: grey metal | colourless gas
Row D: grey metal | brown gas
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

What is seen at each electrode?

A  brown gas at electrode X, grey metal at electrode Y
B  colourless gas at electrode X, grey metal at electrode Y
C  grey metal at electrode X, colourless gas at electrode Y
D  grey metal at electrode X, brown gas at electrode Y

The diagram shows an experiment to electroplate a nickel spoon with silver.

[DIAGRAM – ELECTROPLATING APPARATUS AND TABLE]
A circuit diagram: a power supply connected to two electrodes in an electrolyte solution. The nickel spoon is on the right side. The left electrode is unlabelled.
Below: a table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'positive electrode', Column 2: 'negative electrode', Column 3: 'electrolyte'
Row A: nickel spoon | pure nickel | silver nitrate solution
Row B: nickel spoon | pure silver | nickel nitrate solution
Row C: pure nickel | nickel spoon | silver nitrate solution
Row D: pure silver | nickel spoon | silver nitrate solution
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which row correctly describes the positive electrode, the negative electrode and the electrolyte?

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

The electrical energy, or voltage, of two simple cells is measured.

[DIAGRAM – TWO ELECTROCHEMICAL CELLS]
Cell 1: a voltmeter (V) connected to two electrodes — zinc (left) and magnesium (right) — both dipping into an electrolyte solution.
Cell 2: a voltmeter (V) connected to two electrodes — magnesium (left) and copper (right) — both dipping into the same electrolyte.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which statement correctly describes the results of the experiment?

A  The voltage of cell 1 is greater than cell 2.
B  The electrolyte gradually turns blue in cell 2.
C  Electrons flow from zinc to magnesium in cell 1.
D  Magnesium loses electrons and undergoes oxidation in both cells.

Sodium and rubidium are elements in Group 1 of the Periodic Table.

Which statement is correct?

A  Sodium atoms have more electrons than rubidium atoms.
B  Sodium has a lower density than rubidium.
C  Sodium has a lower melting point than rubidium.
D  Sodium is more reactive than rubidium.

Each beaker contains two strips of metal fastened together and immersed in hydrochloric acid. All the strips are of the same size.

[DIAGRAM – FOUR BEAKERS]
Four beakers labelled A, B, C and D, each containing hydrochloric acid with two metal strips fastened together.
Beaker A: magnesium and zinc strips.
Beaker B: lead and zinc strips.
Beaker C: iron and zinc strips.
Beaker D: copper and zinc strips.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

After 5 minutes, which beaker contains the least amount of zinc ions?

A  beaker A
B  beaker B
C  beaker C
D  beaker D

Three metal carbonates were each heated as shown below.

[DIAGRAM – HEATING APPARATUS AND TABLE]
A test tube containing a metal carbonate, heated by a Bunsen burner. A delivery tube leads from the test tube into a beaker of limewater.
On mild heating of the carbonate of Y, a white precipitate formed in the limewater. Heating more strongly gave the same observation for the carbonate of X but not for the carbonate of Z.
Below: a table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'X', Column 2: 'Y', Column 3: 'Z'
Row A: Zn | Cu | Na
Row B: Zn | Na | Cu
Row C: Na | Zn | Cu
Row D: Na | Cu | Zn
Recommended rendering tool: SVG for apparatus, SVG table for data.

What could X, Y and Z be?

A  X = Zn, Y = Cu, Z = Na
B  X = Zn, Y = Na, Z = Cu
C  X = Na, Y = Zn, Z = Cu
D  X = Na, Y = Cu, Z = Zn

25 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid reacts with excess of a solid to produce a gas. The graph labelled 'first experiment' shows the volume of gas produced over time. Graphs P and Q show the volume of gas produced under different conditions.

[DIAGRAM – RATE OF REACTION GRAPH]
A line graph. Y-axis: 'volume of gas/ cm³'. X-axis: 'time/ s'. Three curves are shown: 'first experiment' (middle curve — moderate rise reaching a plateau); curve P (steeper rise reaching a higher plateau than the first experiment); curve Q (slower rise reaching a lower plateau than the first experiment). All curves begin at the origin.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which changes in conditions produce graphs P and Q, if all other conditions are kept the same?

A  P uses a catalyst and Q has a lower temperature.
B  P uses 25 cm³ of more concentrated acid and Q uses smaller pieces of solid.
C  P uses a higher temperature and Q uses 25 cm³ of 0.5 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid.
D  P uses smaller pieces of solid and Q uses larger pieces of solid.

Petroleum (crude oil) is separated into useful fractions by fractional distillation. The positions at which fractions X and Y are collected from the fractionating column are shown.

[DIAGRAM – FRACTIONATING COLUMN]
A fractionating column with petroleum entering at the bottom. Various fractions exit at different heights via horizontal arrows. Fraction X exits from the upper section of the column (higher position). Fraction Y exits from a lower position below X. Additional fractions exit at the very top and at the bottom.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which statement is correct?

A  The temperature increases up the column.
B  X condenses at a lower temperature than Y.
C  X has a higher boiling point than Y.
D  X has longer chain molecules than Y.
